data.description:
## Context
Audit how the artifact-specific concision guidance recorded by inanimate-unrideable-wasp maps to documentation and durable records in the current rebar project.

## Approach
- Read the canonical documentation policy and indexes, then inspect representative examples of agent guidance, executable-plan guidance, ADRs, user-facing guides, generated reference/API documentation, incident/security material, templates/prompts, ticket comments, and session logs.
- For each artifact class, compare its stated purpose and observed structure with the proposed contract: minimum sufficient content, progressive disclosure, protected facts, current-versus-historical state, alternatives, evidence, and resumption information.
- Classify each class as typically following, partially following, or intentionally not following the guidance. Describe concrete deviations and whether they are defects or purpose-driven exceptions.
- Cite exact repository files and use the existing historical-ticket calibration for tracker artifacts.

## Artifacts
- A concise answer with repository citations.
- A ticket comment recording the audit result.
- No repository files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The answer covers canonical agent guidance, executable tickets/plans, comments/handoffs, ADRs, user-facing documentation, reference/API documentation, incident/security records, and session logs/research notes.
- [ ] Each artifact class has a follows/partially follows/does-not-follow classification.
- [ ] Each non-following or partial class names the specific ways it diverges.
- [ ] Purpose-driven exceptions are distinguished from bloat defects.
- [ ] Claims about repository documentation cite current files.
- [ ] No repository files are modified.

## Verification
Cross-check classifications against docs/documentation-policy.md, docs/README.md, representative files from each artifact class, and the completed 20-ticket calibration.
data.title: Audit concision guidance against current project artifacts
